title: I Reported the Fake Out-of-Order Elevator That Only Served Management

parts.text: I climbed four flights at 8:06 a.m. because the elevator had a fresh OUT OF ORDER sign in Comic Sans. My knees clicked. I was forty-two, carrying a laptop bag and a birthday cake that was starting to lean. On four I saw the COO step out of the same elevator with a coffee that had not climbed stairs. The sign was magnetic. I pulled it off. The elevator worked. I put the sign in my bag, rode down, and watched the COO's assistant slap it back on when the doors closed. I photographed the assistant, the magnet, and the cake. Facilities Slack said no outage ticket existed. Then the assistant sent a floor email: elevator reserved for client tours until further notice. There were no clients on the calendar.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: No ticket, no clients, and a magnetic sign that appears only for the rest of us.

social.video_title: The elevator worked for the COO's coffee — Part 1/2
social.description: Four flights, a leaning cake, and Comic Sans on a magnet. The calendar had no clients. Would you have ridden it anyway?

parts.text: I filed a safety report: false out-of-order signage on a conveyance. Facilities hates that sentence. They pulled badge logs. The elevator had twenty-two management rides during the "outage." The sign was banned. The assistant was reminded that magnets are not work orders. I brought the cake up in the elevator like a person. It stopped leaning. The COO took a slice in the kitchen and said nothing about stairs. I keep a photo of Comic Sans in a folder named conveyance. My knees are quieter. The doors open for everyone, which is what doors are for.

social.video_title: Badge logs showed twenty-two executive rides — Part 2/2
social.description: Safety report, no work order, cake delivered upright. Was a magnet ever an outage?
